methodology: false-merge rate = hand-labeled-wrong / total merge_proposed (the positive set) -- 32-RESEARCH.md 'Don't Hand-Roll' framing. NOT / total O(n^2) pair-space.

labels.rationale: recording_a and recording_b share an IDENTICAL start timestamp to the second (2026-06-16T13:07:12Z) and full participant_overlap (1.0). Two independent recordings cannot start at the exact same instant with the exact same attendees unless they are two different capture tools recording the SAME live call -- this is structurally impossible for two different weekly occurrences of a recurring meeting (those would differ by ~days). The titles describe the same event in two different naming conventions: 'MM.DD.YY - Clickable - Sales Meeting' (manual/legacy style) vs 'YYYY-MM-DD-clickable-sales-meeting' (auto-slugified style), consistent with two different recording sources capturing one real-world meeting. Genuine merge candidate.

Same reasoning as the 06/16 pair: identical start timestamp to the second (2026-06-17T13:25:55Z), full participant_overlap (1.0), same event described in two title formats, one day later in the same recurring sales-meeting series. Since each pair's own two members share an exact-second timestamp (not ~24h or ~7d apart), this is two captures of one meeting, not two different series occurrences being wrongly conflated -- the exact failure mode (F5 / recurring-instance false-merge) this milestone's MATCH-04/05 hardening and the metadata tier's title_suppressed logic exist to prevent. title_suppressed=false is correct here precisely because the strong independent time+participant signals justify the merge on their own, not on title-recurrence alone. Genuine merge candidate.

false_merge_rate.sample_size_caveat: n=2 is a very small sample -- this org has 249 recordings but only 2 pairs crossed the metadata tier's MERGE_PROPOSE_THRESHOLD (0.80) in this sweep. 0/2 = 0% is well under the <=0.1% target and both proposals are high-confidence genuine matches on inspection (exact-second time overlap + full participant overlap), but n=2 is not a statistically powerful bound at the 0.1% threshold on its own. The flag stays enabled for this org so more real proposals accumulate over time (see Deviations for the cron-scheduling gap found and its current status).
